model.rationale: A D+21 electorate, an incumbent with roughly a hundred-to-one cash-on-hand edge, no outside spending against her, and markets pricing her win at 96 percent all point to a safe Democratic hold, so the forecast sits near fundamentals at a margin of about 25 points.

notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
California's 30th District leans Democratic by 21 points, and Democrat Laura Friedman holds the seat as the incumbent. She has raised nearly $1 million and reports about $520,000 in cash on hand, while Republican Scott Meyers has raised roughly $123,000 and reports only about $5,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Friedman, and no general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race.

Prediction markets price a Friedman win at roughly 96 percent. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage leaves Meyers with little visible path. The forecast expects Friedman to win by a wide margin, with uncertainty somewhat elevated because polling is absent and turnout in low-profile general elections can vary.
